title: Gridz Attestation Envelope
description: A portable, self-describing reference to the signed attestation that backs a cell or a Grid root. Verification of an attestation MUST NOT require trusting any sink, server, or vault: a consumer with only (subject did, attester public key, this envelope, value) can verify. Sinks are projections, not sources of truth.

hash32.description: 32-byte hash, lowercase hex with 0x prefix (keccak256 on EVM, sha256 on non-EVM; see specs/canonicalization.md).

uri.description: Location of the raw attestation. Supported schemes include eas:, eth:, ipfs:, ar:, https:, and data:. eas: URIs take the form eas://<chainId>/<uid>.

format.description: How the attestation was produced. eip712-oneclaw is byte-for-byte identical to eip712-raw at verification time; the suffix records provenance only and carries no trust weight.

uid.description: Unique attestation identifier: the EAS uid for eas-*, the JWS jti for jws-ed25519, a derived hash for the others. Used as the merkle leaf for the Grid root.

attester.description: DID of the signer. The recovered/verified public key MUST resolve to this DID, else verification fails.

exp.description: Optional expiry (ISO-8601). Mirrors the cell's expires_at when set.

value_hash.description: Hash of the canonicalized signed value: keccak256(JCS(cell.value)) on EVM, sha256(JCS(cell.value)) on non-EVM. For a root attestation this is the merkle root over cell UIDs.

revocation.description: Optional revocation pointer. Absence does not imply non-revocable; eas-* formats are revocable via the schema's revocable flag.

payload.description: Optional raw signed payload, base64url-encoded. Lets a verifier check the attestation fully offline without dereferencing uri.

then.$comment: COSE/WebAuthn attestations attest a value_hash via the authenticator; attester DID is typically did:key derived from the credential public key.
